guarantees.claim: For all x and y in 0..4, result[x][y][W-1:0] is assigned the value state[PiRotate[x][y]][x][W-1:0].

assumptions.claim: Every entry PiRotate[x][y] must be an integer in the range 0..4.
assumptions.risk: Out-of-bounds array access on state would produce X-propagation or undefined simulation behavior, corrupting the Keccak state.

uncertain_points.claim: The PiRotate lookup table must implement the correct Keccak-pi permutation (x+3y mod 5, or equivalent) to maintain cryptographic diffusion properties.
uncertain_points.risk: A wrong permutation would break the Keccak sponge construction, potentially weakening or breaking the security of the hash/duplex output.

uncertain_points.claim: If the parameter W can be set to 0, the part-select [W-1:0] becomes an invalid range, causing a simulation error or undefined behavior.
uncertain_points.risk: Logic may not be synthesizable or could cause X propagation in simulation; in an RTL crypto core this would be a fundamental misuse.
